text:
maria: heads up — CI started failing for the edge-runtime unit tests in both vitest and jest. Seems like mocks for global fetch + kv store are flaky under ESM. Example failure from nightly attached.

ci-bot: nightly-edge-tests · build/edge-tests #482 failed — log excerpt:
```
Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at Object.compileFunction (node:vm:360:18)
    at wrapSafe (internal/modules/cjs/loader:1054:15)
    at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader:1092:27)
    at Object.Module._extensions..js (internal/modules/cjs/loader:1180:10)
    at Module.load (internal/modules/cjs/loader:1004:32)
```

alex: I think this comes from our test bootstrap loading CJS mocks while the SDK package is published as ESM ("type": "module"). Jest's transform config and vitest's resolver handle conditional exports differently. Seen this with fetch polyfills before.

tyler: quick repro: run `pnpm -w test --filter @redwood/sdk -- run edge` with `type:module` — vitest fails to mock `./runtime/fetch` because vite's resolver inlines the package entrypoint. If you switch tests to import the CJS shim directly it passes.

jamie: we have conditional exports in package.json ("exports": {"./runtime": {"import":"./dist/runtime.mjs","require":"./dist/runtime.cjs"}}) — vitest picks the import path, jest (with transformIgnorePatterns) sometimes resolves to cjs, so mocks get attached to a different module identity.

maria: proposed workaround I tested locally (works for our CI job):

1) vitest.config.ts tweaks:
```ts
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    deps: { inline: ['@redwood/sdk'] },
    transformMode: { web: [/\.m?[jt]s$/] },
  }
})
```
2) jest.config.js tweaks (if you run jest):
```js
module.exports = {
  transformIgnorePatterns: ['node_modules/(?!@redwood/sdk)'],
  moduleNameMapper: { '^@redwood/sdk$': '<rootDir>/dist/runtime.cjs' }
}
```
Or as an alternative add a tiny ESM-compatible test shim that uses `createRequire` to load the CJS mock so both runners see the same module identity. Example shim (tests/setup/require-shim.cjs):
```js
const { createRequire } = require('module');
const req = createRequire(import.meta.url || __filename);
module.exports = req('../dist/runtime.cjs');
```

alex: another lightweight option is to ship test-only `exports` mapping in package.json behind an env var in CI, but that's a bit gross. The shim + inline deps is the least invasive.

tyler: opened PR to our mono repo with the prov config + a small test shim: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/478 — includes CI patch to `pnpm -w test` that inlines the sdk for vitest and maps the module for jest.

jamie: confirmed on my branch, CI passed on linux + mac runners. windows still flaky but likely newline/import quirks.

maria: thanks all. I pushed the quickfix to the edge-tests pipeline. Re-run scheduled. If you see a different failure please paste the exact stack. :thumbsup:

alex: follow-up: we should add a small doc in devex about ESM/CJS test pitfalls and recommend either "inline deps" for vitest or the shim pattern. I'll draft it.

maria: sounds good, closing this thread for now. reopen if it resurfaces. :white_check_mark:
